items.note: The first word of the book, and the tail end of its last sentence.
No apostrophe. Joyce kept the title secret for years and called it Work in Progress.
The hill on Dublin Bay. Most visitors say it wrong, rhyming it with mouth.
Vico, the philosopher, is said VEE-ko. Vico Road runs along the coast south of Dublin.
Usually just HCE, said as three letters.
Anna Livia comes from the Liffey, Dublin's river.
The river through Dublin. ALP is the river.
The village where HCE keeps his pub. By tradition, Isolde's chapel.
The rival twins. Shaun is the Irish Sean.
The daughter, Isabel. A mirror for Isolde.
The giant of Irish legend, in Irish Fionn mac Cumhaill. He sleeps under Dublin in the book.
A pun on French perce-oreille, earwig: pairss-or-AY.
Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, squeezed into one name for the Four Old Men.
Joyce's line rhymes quark with Mark. Physicists often say kwork instead.
The museum in I.1, read with a lilt.
The stolen children in the Prankquean tale. Tristram plus Christopher; sad and cheerful.
